letters.name: alef
letters.memoryTrick: Tall standing stick — the first letter, like 'A' at attention. Makes a long 'ah' as in 'father'. At the start of a word it often carries a tiny 'آ' (alef with hat) for the 'â' sound.

letters.name: be
letters.memoryTrick: A boat-shaped bowl with ONE dot below — B for Boat, dot Below. Easy: one dot under = 'b'.

letters.name: pe
letters.memoryTrick: Same bowl as 'be' but with THREE dots below — P for Pe, three dots like a Puddle. Unique to Farsi! Not found in Arabic.

letters.name: te
letters.memoryTrick: Bowl with TWO dots above — T for Te, Two dots on Top. The two dots look like little eyes looking down.

letters.name: se
letters.memoryTrick: Bowl with THREE dots above in a triangle — think 'three' for 's' (se sounds like 'say'). Rare in native Farsi words; mostly appears in Arabic loanwords.

letters.name: jim
letters.memoryTrick: Curves like a 'J' hook with a single dot nestled inside. J for Jim — the dot sits inside the curve like a jewel.

letters.name: che
letters.memoryTrick: Same hook as jim but with THREE dots inside — CH for Che, three dots = CHocolate chips. Unique to Farsi!

letters.name: he-ye jimi
letters.memoryTrick: A smooth loop with NO dots — think 'Hello' with an H. Makes a stronger, breathier 'h' from the chest. 'Jimi' means 'like jim' because of its similar shape.

letters.name: khe
letters.memoryTrick: Same loop as he-ye jimi but with ONE dot above — the dot is like a scratch mark. Makes the throaty 'kh' sound, like the 'ch' in Scottish 'loch' or German 'Bach'.

letters.name: dâl
letters.memoryTrick: A simple D-shaped curve with a small hook. D for Dâl. It does NOT connect to the following letter — it stands alone on the left side.

letters.name: zâl
letters.memoryTrick: Same shape as dâl but with ONE dot above — like dâl wearing a little hat. Makes a 'z' sound. Rarely starts words; mostly found in Arabic loanwords.

letters.name: re
letters.memoryTrick: A small curving R-shape that dips below the line. R for Re. Like dâl, it does NOT connect to the following letter — it keeps its space.

letters.name: ze
letters.memoryTrick: Same shape as re but with ONE dot above — Z for Ze. A buzzy 'z' like the 'z' in 'zebra'. Also a non-connector.

letters.name: zhe
letters.memoryTrick: Re with THREE dots above — like zhuzh (styling gel)! Makes the 'zh' sound, like the 's' in 'pleasure' or 'j' in French 'bonjour'. Unique to Farsi!

letters.name: sin
letters.memoryTrick: Three little teeth in a row — s-s-s like a snake hissing through its teeth! No dots, just the three connected peaks in a line.

letters.name: shin
letters.memoryTrick: Three teeth like 'sin' but with THREE dots above in a triangle — SH for Shin, like 'SHhhh' putting three fingers to your lips.

letters.name: sâd
letters.memoryTrick: A closed loop that drops below the line — makes the same 's' sound as 'sin'. Think of it as a 'heavy S'. Mostly appears in Arabic loanwords.

letters.name: zâd
letters.memoryTrick: Sâd with ONE dot above — the dot turns the 's' into a 'z'. Makes the same 'z' as 'ze'. Rare at the start of words; appears mostly in Arabic loans.

letters.name: tâ
letters.memoryTrick: A loop with a vertical line through it — like a 'T' wrapped in a circle. Makes the same 't' sound as 'te'. A 'heavy T' used in Arabic loanwords.

letters.name: zâ
letters.memoryTrick: Tâ with ONE dot above — the dot turns 't' into 'z'. Very rare at the start of words. Same 'z' sound as the other Z letters.

letters.name: eyn
letters.memoryTrick: Looks like an eye or a little cradle. In Farsi it's often a soft glottal stop or merges into a short 'a/e' vowel. Think of it as a little breath catch in your throat.

letters.name: qeyn
letters.memoryTrick: Eyn with ONE dot above — the dot 'scratches' the sound! Makes a gargling 'gh' like the French 'r' in 'Paris'. Imagine clearing your throat very gently.

letters.name: fe
letters.memoryTrick: A round F-shape with ONE dot above — F for Fe, the dot floats above like a flag on a pole.

letters.name: qâf
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'fe' but with TWO dots above and a longer tail. Makes a deep 'q/gh' from the back of the throat — Q for Qâf. In Tehrani Farsi it often sounds like 'gh'.

letters.name: kâf
letters.memoryTrick: Looks like a K-shape with a stroke above. K for Kâf. In Farsi, kâf always has this distinctive diagonal stroke on top (the 'sar-e kâf'), unlike Arabic kaf.

letters.name: gâf
letters.memoryTrick: Kâf with an EXTRA stroke (two parallel strokes instead of one) — G for Gâf, the extra stroke gives it extra 'g' power! Unique to Farsi!

letters.name: lâm
letters.memoryTrick: A tall L-shaped stroke — L for Lâm, it stands tall like a lamppost. One of the most recognizable letters in the script.

letters.name: mim
letters.memoryTrick: A little loop that hangs down with a tail — M for Mim. Looks like a Mermaid tail dipping below the line.

letters.name: nun
letters.memoryTrick: A curved bowl with ONE dot above — N for Nun, the dot above like a Notch. Makes the same 'n' as English.

letters.name: vâv
letters.memoryTrick: A small loop like a V-shape opening — V for Vâv. Acts as both a consonant ('v') and a vowel ('u' or 'ow' sound). Non-connector — it never joins to the left.

letters.name: he-ye do-cheshm
letters.memoryTrick: Looks like TWO EYES ('do-cheshm' means 'two eyes'!). Makes a soft 'h' or, at the end of a word, an '-e' sound (like the 'e' in 'bed').

letters.name: ye
letters.memoryTrick: A graceful curve with TWO dots below — Y for Ye. Works as a consonant ('y' as in 'yes') or a vowel ('i' as in 'ski'). Two dots, two roles!

letters.name: zebar (fathe)
letters.romanization: a (short vowel mark placed above a letter)
letters.memoryTrick: A tiny diagonal stroke ABOVE a letter — like a little hat that says 'a'! Called 'zebar' in Farsi. Rarely written in everyday text but essential for learners.

letters.name: zir (kasre)
letters.romanization: e (short vowel mark placed below a letter)
letters.memoryTrick: A tiny diagonal stroke BELOW a letter — 'zir' even means 'under' in Farsi! Makes the short 'e' sound like in 'bed'.

letters.name: pish (zamme)
letters.romanization: o (short vowel mark placed above a letter)
letters.memoryTrick: A tiny loop ABOVE a letter — looks like a little 'o' mouth! Makes the short 'o' sound like in 'go' (but shorter). Called 'pish' in Farsi.
